title: Ye Islands of the Northern Sea
description: Ye Islands of the Northern Sea in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 97, part 4, headed “Christ's incarnation, and the last judgment”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ye is-lands of the north-ern sea, Re-joice, the Sa-viour reigns; His word like fire, pre-pares his way, And moun-tains melt to plains.

lines: Ye islands of the northern sea,
Rejoice, the Saviour reigns;
His word like fire, prepares his way,
And mountains melt to plains.
His presence sinks the proudest hills,
And makes the vallies rise
The humble soul enjoys his smiles,
The haughty sinner dies.
The heavens his rightful power proclaim
The idol-gods around
Fill their own worshippers with shame,
And totter to the ground.
Adoring angels at his birth
Make the Redeemer known;
Thus shall he come to judge the earth,
And angels guard his throne.
His foes shall tremble at his sight,
And hills and seas retire
His children take their unknown flight,
And leave the world in fire.
The seeds of joy and glory sown
For saints in darkness here
Shall rise and spring in worlds unknown,
And a rich harvest bear.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
